description: Golden dataset for evaluating the Natively Legal RAG pipeline. Each question simulates a real client question during a lawyer consultation.

questions.clientQuestion: My brother grabbed the ancestral land, what can I do?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You have a right to seek partition of the ancestral property

questions.clientQuestion: Can I take back the gift I gave to my son last year?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A gift can only be revoked if there was a prior agreement or condition

questions.clientQuestion: What is a gift deed and how is it different from a will?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A gift takes effect during the donor's lifetime while a will operates after death

questions.clientQuestion: My father gifted the house but kept living there. Now he passed away and my uncle says the gift was invalid because there was no delivery.
questions.expectedBottomLine: For immovable property, a registered gift deed constitutes valid transfer even without physical delivery

questions.clientQuestion: My father died without a will. Who gets his property?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Property devolves on Class I heirs simultaneously and equally

questions.clientQuestion: Does my daughter have the same rights as my son in the family property?
questions.expectedBottomLine: After the 2005 amendment, daughters have equal coparcenary rights as sons

questions.clientQuestion: Someone is about to sell the property that we are disputing in court. Can we stop the sale?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can apply for a temporary injunction under Order XXXIX to restrain the sale

questions.clientQuestion: How long does a civil suit usually take and what is the process?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A civil suit begins with filing a plaint and follows stages of pleadings, framing of issues, evidence, and decree

questions.clientQuestion: I want to set up a trust for my children's education. What do I need?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You need a trust deed specifying the trustee, beneficiaries, trust property, and the purpose

questions.clientQuestion: Can I remove the trustee if he is mismanaging the trust funds?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A trustee can be removed by the court for breach of trust or mismanagement

questions.clientQuestion: What documents do I need to buy a flat?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You need a registered sale deed, title verification, encumbrance certificate, and payment of stamp duty

questions.clientQuestion: My tenant has not paid rent for 6 months but refuses to leave. What can I do?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can issue a notice of termination and file an eviction suit for non-payment of rent

questions.clientQuestion: I am an NRI. Can I buy agricultural land in India?
questions.expectedBottomLine: NRIs cannot acquire agricultural land, plantation property, or farmhouse in India without RBI approval

questions.clientQuestion: Can I send money to my family in India from abroad? Is there a limit?
questions.expectedBottomLine: There is no limit on inward remittances to India, but outward remittances are subject to the Liberalized Remittance Scheme limit

questions.clientQuestion: Can I disinherit one of my children in my will?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can disinherit any legal heir from self-acquired property through a valid will

questions.clientQuestion: My mother made a will but she had Alzheimer's. Can we challenge it?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A will can be challenged if the testator lacked mental capacity to understand its nature and effects at the time of making it

questions.clientQuestion: Someone has been illegally occupying my land for 15 years. Have I lost my rights?
questions.expectedBottomLine: After 12 years of continuous, open, and hostile possession, the occupier may claim title by adverse possession

questions.clientQuestion: I won the case but the other party is not following the court order. What can I do?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can file an execution petition under Order XXI to enforce the decree

questions.clientQuestion: My neighbour built a wall on my land. I have the documents to prove it's my land. What should I do?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can file a suit for recovery of possession and mandatory injunction to remove the encroachment

questions.clientQuestion: What happens if two wills exist and they say different things?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A later will revokes the earlier will to the extent of any inconsistency

questions.clientQuestion: Can I sell my share in a jointly owned property without the other owner's consent?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A co-owner can sell their undivided share without the consent of other co-owners

questions.clientQuestion: I lost the case in district court. Can I go to a higher court?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You have a right to file a first appeal against the decree in the High Court

questions.clientQuestion: I paid the full price for a flat but the builder hasn't given me possession or the deed. What are my options?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Under the doctrine of part performance, you can claim protection and file a suit for specific performance

questions.clientQuestion: What is the difference between a public trust and a private trust?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A private trust is for specific individuals while a public trust benefits the general public or a section of it

questions.clientQuestion: My husband died and his family says I have no right to his property because we had a love marriage.
questions.expectedBottomLine: As a legally married wife, you are a Class I heir and have equal right to your husband's property regardless of marriage type

questions.clientQuestion: Someone is sending me threatening messages. Can I file a case?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can file an FIR for criminal intimidation and if done online, also under IT Act provisions

questions.clientQuestion: I gave someone power of attorney to manage my property. Can they sell it without asking me?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Only if the power of attorney specifically authorizes sale; a general POA does not automatically include sale authority

questions.clientQuestion: My father is an NRI and wants to transfer his Indian property to me. Is there any restriction?
questions.expectedBottomLine: An NRI can gift or sell residential and commercial property to a person resident in India

questions.clientQuestion: The other party in my case keeps getting adjournments. Can I do anything to speed up the trial?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can oppose adjournments, seek costs for delay, and request the court to fix a strict timeline

questions.clientQuestion: What is the difference between a lease and a license for my shop?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A lease creates an interest in property with exclusive possession while a license merely permits use without creating any interest

questions.clientQuestion: How do I write a will? Do I need a lawyer?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A will must be signed by the testator and attested by two witnesses; a lawyer is not legally required but recommended

questions.clientQuestion: I sold my property but now the buyer says there are old debts attached to it. Am I liable?
questions.expectedBottomLine: The seller has a duty to disclose material defects and known encumbrances; undisclosed charges may make the sale voidable

questions.clientQuestion: Can a trust own property in its own name?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Trust property is held in the name of the trustee for the benefit of the beneficiary; the trust itself is not a legal person

questions.clientQuestion: Can we settle the case out of court even after the case has been filed?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Yes, parties can settle at any stage through mediation, lok adalat, or by recording a compromise decree

questions.clientQuestion: Someone forged my father's signature on a sale deed. What can I do?
questions.expectedBottomLine: A forged deed is void ab initio and you can file a suit for declaration and cancellation of the fraudulent document

questions.clientQuestion: My father had two wives. How will his property be divided?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Both widows are Class I heirs and will receive equal shares along with children

questions.clientQuestion: What is stamp duty and who pays it?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Stamp duty is a tax on property transactions typically paid by the buyer at rates set by the state government

questions.clientQuestion: I filed a case but the court says it doesn't have jurisdiction. What does that mean?
questions.expectedBottomLine: Jurisdiction determines which court can hear your case based on location, value, and subject matter of the dispute

questions.clientQuestion: My builder is not completing the construction on time. What legal action can I take?
questions.expectedBottomLine: You can file a complaint under RERA for delay and seek compensation or refund with interest

questions.clientQuestion: Can an adopted child inherit property from the biological parents?
questions.expectedBottomLine: An adopted child loses inheritance rights from biological parents and acquires rights in the adoptive family
